subject: Re: Private Offer — early-adopter credit & channel margin proposal
messages:
From: Samir Bose <samir@cloudscale.com>

Cc: procurement@acme-enterprises.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer — request for early-adopter credit + channel margin

Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. CloudScale is close to selecting a vendor for our in-app assistant; procurement asked me to surface Redwood's private-offer terms so we can complete the business review next week. Two asks from my side:

- Early-adopter one-time credit (to offset integration costs) — target: $75k
- Channel margin for our marketplace/reseller flow (we need a minimum of 18% to keep economics for our partners)

We plan to commit to an initial 12-month consumption minimum of $420k (list) with an option to expand. Can Redwood map what that credit + channel margin would look like by Monday? Procurement (cc) will want a draft PO and pricing table to kick off legal.

Happy to run a quick call if it helps.

—Samir
Samir Bose
Head of Cloud Partnerships, CloudScale
samir@cloudscale.com

Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Private offer — request for early-adopter credit + channel margin

Team — forwarding CloudScale's asks below. They called out: $75k one-time credit + 18% channel margin tied to our marketplace/reseller flow. They propose a 12-month engagement around $420k list.

Proposed approach (initial thinking):
- Offer a tiered early-adopter credit: $50k base, + $25k uplift when commit >= $500k ARR
- Channel margin: 18% for first 12 months, step-down to 12% thereafter unless partner commit increases
- Require a signed private offer + PO; credit applied as single invoice credit after month 1

Attaching a draft pricing matrix (pricing_matrix.xlsx) with modeled net ARR and margin impact. Rafael — pls advise on maximum concession we can approve for AE-led deals. Marissa — can you flag any marketplace constraints (billing, invoice flows) we should surface to procurement?

Thanks,
Ben

From: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private offer — request for early-adopter credit + channel margin

Ben —

I reviewed the attachment; baseline guidance from finance:
- Early-adopter credit: we can approve up to $75k one-time but recommend structuring as $50k guaranteed + $25k contingent on a $500k net ARR threshold to protect unit economics.
- Channel margin: 18% is acceptable for the first 12 months for marketplace/reseller flows, provided we include a clause that reverts margin to 12% post-first-year unless CloudScale secures a defined partner commit or growth metric.
- All credits must be amortized over the first 6 invoice periods and applied as invoice credits — no cash refunds.

I've attached a redline of the draft PO (PO_Draft_v2.pdf) with the recommended language (payments, credit amortization, rollback clause). Note: if we make the full $75k unconditional, blended unit economics drop ~6-8% at $420k ARR; the contingency protects margins.

Approve if you want me to provisionally sign finance approval so legal can start drafting language.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private offer — request for early-adopter credit + channel margin

All —

Echo Rafael's recommendation. A couple of operational asks from Marketplace & Ops:
- If we grant 18% margin, we need CloudScale to commit to using the official marketplace SKU for the first 12 months; otherwise tracking and pass-through invoicing will be messy.
- Reduce unconditional credit to $50k; unlock the +$25k when they submit a signed statement of expected consumption and a PO >= $500k. That keeps legal/ops overhead lower.
- Ask legal to include a simple audit right to validate partner-reported usage for the channel ack.

If we agree to contingent structure, I'm OK routing to Legal + Procurement and pushing a firm PO template to CloudScale.

Marissa Cole
Head of Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Bose <samir@cloudscale.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@acme-enterprises.com>, procurement@acme-enterprises.com
Cc: rafael_mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer — request for early-adopter credit + channel margin

Samir / Elena / procurement team —

Thanks for the patience. Based on internal alignment, here is Redwood's proposed private-offer structure for CloudScale:

1) Early-adopter credit: $50,000 guaranteed + $25,000 contingent when cumulative committed ARR >= $500,000 within the first 30 days of the private offer. Credit is applied as invoice credit amortized over the first 6 invoices.

2) Channel margin: 18% for the first 12 months for marketplace/reseller flows, reverting to 12% thereafter unless a partner commit metric is met (we can define the metric in contract).

3) Operational requirements: CloudScale must use the official marketplace SKU for billing during the first 12 months and provide a signed statement of expected consumption. Redwood retains an audit right for partner-reported usage tied to margin eligibility.

Attached are: pricing_matrix.xlsx (net vs list scenarios) and PO_Draft_v2.pdf (contains the margin and credit language). We can push a DocuSign link for the private offer when you're ready: https://docusign.net/tx/CloudScale_PO_12345

Next steps: please confirm whether CloudScale will sign the PO by Tue, Jul 5 so we can reserve the early-adopter credits and enable marketplace routing. Happy to jump on 30 minutes to walk legal/procurement through the contract language.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Exec — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
